method: A tempo fixes the length of a musical beat: one beat lasts 60 / BPM seconds and one bar lasts that beat times the beats per bar, so 120 BPM in 4/4 gives a 500 ms beat and a 2 s bar. At a project frame rate the same beat is beat seconds x frames per second long; the page lists that value exactly, then places each requested cut on the nearest whole frame and reports the frame number, the SMPTE timecode built from that frame index, and the distance in milliseconds between the cut and the exact beat. Cuts can be listed every beat, every bar, every 2 bars or every 4 bars, with an optional first-beat offset in seconds or minutes:seconds, and the plan covers 1 to 64 bars. Placing every cut independently on the nearest frame keeps the error bounded by half a frame (about 20.8 ms at 24 fps) rather than accumulating, while holding one whole number of frames per gap accumulates: the page reports that fixed-spacing drift at the last cut. Timecode uses the nominal rate, with drop-frame labels at 29.97 and 59.94 that skip frame numbers at the top of each minute except every tenth, and standard non-drop labels at 23.976, which run about 0.1% behind wall-clock time. Tempo is limited to 20-300 BPM, bars to 1-64, the offset to 0-600 s and the list to 240 cut points. The page does not detect beats, and live performance drifts away from a click, so the plan is a starting point to check against the waveform. Everything is computed in the browser with no uploads, network access or storage.

sources.title: A beat at a given tempo lasts 60 / BPM seconds, and a bar is that beat multiplied by the beats per bar; this is the standard relation between tempo, note value and duration used by DAWs and notation software.

Frame rate converts a duration into frames: a time in seconds multiplied by frames per second gives the frame position, and rounding to the nearest whole frame bounds the quantisation error by half a frame.

SMPTE timecode labels a frame index as hours:minutes:seconds:frames, and drop-frame counting at 29.97 and 59.94 skips frame numbers at the top of each minute except every tenth so the label follows the clock.
